issue_request: FHIR-19597 asked the core search page to clarify expected behavior when a Quantity search supplies a unit code without a system, especially whether Quantity.code, Quantity.unit, or both should be considered. Jira status is Published with Persuasive resolution, raised in STU3 and applied for R5.
initial_application: Git commit 7c9884b2adc8f3a572d8ca491f2be92f5e76a90e, titled 'FHIR-19597 - Clarify system-less quantity search.', updated source/search.html to add explicit Quantity search syntax forms, including [parameter]={[prefix]}[number]||[code] matching by value and code or unit. Same-day commit 44a2455d847 retained that systemless form in the current ordering.
additional_context: The implementers Zulip thread for 'Quantity search and display units' records the split implementation poll and Lloyd McKenzie's interpretation that code+system searches match Quantity.code plus Quantity.system only, while code-only searches match Quantity.code or Quantity.unit. FHIR-17790 is related background for optional Quantity unit system/code and is already represented on the combined branch. Confluence searches found no direct FHIR-19597 records or contrary work-group context.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source/search.html already states that [parameter]={[prefix]}[number]||[code] matches a quantity by value and code or unit and includes the Observation?value-quantity=5.4||mg example described as matching either Quantity.code or stated human Quantity.unit.

related_jiras.note: Earlier Published issue clarified that Quantity unit system/code are optional and is already represented on the combined branch; it frames but does not supersede the FHIR-19597 systemless code-or-unit rule.
